blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India's vegetation varies from tropical evergreen rainforests in high-rainfall zones to arid thorn scrub in desert regions.
Tropical Deciduous Forests are the most widespread forest cover in India, divided into Moist and Dry Deciduous sub-types.
Tropical Evergreen Forests occur in regions with annual rainfall exceeding 200 cm and maintain year-round green foliage.
Montane forests exhibit a distinct vertical zonation of vegetation matching temperature variations with increasing altitude.
Mangrove forests thrive in coastal tidal regions, dominated by salt-tolerant species like Sundari trees in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.
